answerHeadline: Creation — God Creates the World, Light, Adam & Eve in Six Days
modernSummary: In the beginning God creates heaven, earth, light, stars, oceans, plants, animals, and humanity (Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden) and rests on the seventh day.

answerHeadline: Adam & Eve — Forbidden Fruit, Talking Snake & Leaving Eden
modernSummary: A crafty serpent (snake) tempts Eve and Adam to eat the forbidden fruit from the tree of knowledge of good and evil, bringing sin, shame, and exile from Eden.

answerHeadline: Cain & Abel — First Murder Between Jealous Brothers
modernSummary: Envious that God favored Abel’s offering, Cain kills his brother Abel in the field and asks, “Am I my brother’s keeper?” before being marked and wandering.

answerHeadline: Noah’s Ark — Great Flood, Pairs of Animals & Rainbow Promise
modernSummary: Noah builds a massive wooden boat (ark) to rescue his family and two of every animal from a worldwide flood for 40 days and nights; a dove returns with an olive branch and God sets a rainbow covenant.

answerHeadline: Tower of Babel — Tall City Reaching Heaven & Confused Languages
modernSummary: Humanity builds a giant skyscraper tower trying to reach heaven and make a name for themselves, so God confuses their languages and scatters people across the earth.

answerHeadline: Lot’s Wife — Person Who Turned Into a Pillar of Salt
modernSummary: While angels rush Lot and his family out of burning Sodom and Gomorrah warning them not to look back, Lot’s wife looks behind her and immediately turns into a pillar of salt.

answerHeadline: Abraham & Isaac — Father Willing to Sacrifice His Son on the Mountain
modernSummary: God tests Abraham on Mount Moriah by asking him to offer his beloved son Isaac, then stops Abraham’s hand at the last second and provides a ram caught in a bush.

answerHeadline: Jacob & Esau — Stolen Birthright for a Bowl of Stew
modernSummary: Hairy hunter Esau trades his birthright to his twin brother Jacob for red lentil stew; later Jacob wears goatskins on his arms to trick blind Isaac into giving him the blessing.

answerHeadline: Jacob’s Ladder & Wrestling God at Peniel
modernSummary: Sleeping on a stone pillow, Jacob dreams of angels climbing a stairway to heaven; years later he wrestles an angel all night until his hip is touched and he is renamed Israel.

answerHeadline: Joseph — Colorful Coat, Pit, Egyptian Prison & Forgiving His Brothers
modernSummary: Favored by his father with a multicolored robe, dreamer Joseph is thrown into a dry well and sold into slavery by jealous brothers—yet interprets Pharaoh’s dreams, saves Egypt from famine, and forgives his family.

answerHeadline: Baby Moses — Floating in a Basket Down the Nile River
modernSummary: To save her newborn Hebrew boy from Pharaoh’s decree, Moses’s mother puts him in a waterproof papyrus basket among the reeds where Pharaoh’s daughter adopts him while Miriam watches.

answerHeadline: Moses & the Burning Bush — Fire That Never Consumes the Shrub
modernSummary: Shepherding in Midian, Moses sees a bush ablaze with fire that never burns up; God speaks from the flames (“I AM WHO I AM”) and sends Moses back to free Israel from slavery.

answerHeadline: Ten Plagues of Egypt & Passover Night (Lamb’s Blood on Doorposts)
modernSummary: God sends ten plagues upon Egypt—water to blood, frogs, gnats, flies, darkness—until Passover night when Israelites paint lamb’s blood on doorframes so judgment passes over them.

answerHeadline: Parting the Red Sea — Crossing Dry Ground Between Walls of Water
modernSummary: Trapped between Pharaoh’s chariots and the sea, Moses stretches out his staff; an east wind splits the Red Sea in two so Israel walks across on dry land before waters crash over the chariots.

answerHeadline: Manna & Quail — Food / Bread That Falls From Heaven Every Morning
modernSummary: When freed Israelites starve in the desert, God rains miraculous sweet flaky food called manna down from the sky every morning like dew—plus quail at dusk—so nobody goes hungry.

answerHeadline: Ten Commandments on Stone Tablets & Golden Calf Idol
modernSummary: Amid thunder and fire atop Mount Sinai, God carves the Ten Commandments into stone tablets while Aaron and impatient Israelites melt gold jewelry into a golden calf idol below.

answerHeadline: Twelve Spies, Giant Fruit & Caleb’s Courage
modernSummary: Twelve scouts explore Canaan and bring back a cluster of grapes so big it takes two men on a pole; ten spies panic over giants, while only Joshua and Caleb trust God.

answerHeadline: Bronze Serpent on a Pole — Healing Fiery Snakebites
modernSummary: When venomous snakes bite complaining travelers, God has Moses lift a bronze snake on a pole so anyone who looks up at it is immediately healed.

answerHeadline: Balaam’s Donkey — Animal That Started Talking to Save Its Rider
modernSummary: When Balaam rides off to curse Israel, his loyal donkey sees an armed angel blocking the trail, crushes Balaam’s foot, lies down, and starts talking out loud to rebuke him.

answerHeadline: Rahab & Walls of Jericho — Trumpets, Marching & Scarlet Cord
modernSummary: Rahab hides Israelite spies behind flax and hangs a red rope out her window; then Israel marches around Jericho for seven days until loud shouts and ram horns tumble the stone walls flat.

answerHeadline: Deborah & Jael — Woman Judge and Tent Peg Victory
modernSummary: Prophetess Deborah leads Israel alongside Barak while flash floods stall 900 iron chariots; fleeing general Sisera hides in Jael’s tent where she offers warm milk and drives a tent peg.

answerHeadline: Gideon’s 300 Warriors — Torches Inside Clay Jars & Wet Fleece
modernSummary: Hesitant Gideon asks God for signs on a wool fleece, then trims an army of 32,000 down to 300 men lapping water who rout Midian at night with smashed pitchers, torches, and trumpets.

answerHeadline: Samson & Delilah — Superhuman Hair Strength & Falling Temple Pillars
modernSummary: Long-haired Nazirite strongman Samson kills a lion with bare hands, fights with a donkey jawbone, loses his strength when Delilah shaves his seven braids, then pushes down Philistine pillars.

answerHeadline: Ruth, Naomi & Boaz — Widow Picking Leftover Barley & Loyal Love
modernSummary: Young widow Ruth refuses to leave grieving Naomi (“Wherever you go, I will go”), gleans grain in Bethlehem fields, and marries generous Boaz—becoming King David’s great-grandmother.

answerHeadline: Young Samuel Calling “Speak Lord” in the Night
modernSummary: Sleeping inside the temple at Shiloh, little boy Samuel hears a voice calling his name three times before old priest Eli realizes it is God speaking.

answerHeadline: David & Goliath — Shepherd Boy Killing Giant With Slingshot & Stone
modernSummary: While armored soldiers tremble before giant champion Goliath, young shepherd David picks five smooth creek stones and fells Goliath with a single stone from his sling.

answerHeadline: David & Jonathan — Loyal Friendship, Secret Arrows & Jealous King Saul
modernSummary: Prince Jonathan warns his best friend David of King Saul’s spear-throwing jealousy using prearranged archery signals in a field.

answerHeadline: King Solomon’s Wisdom — Splitting the Baby Between Two Mothers
modernSummary: Asking God for a listening heart instead of riches, King Solomon settles two women arguing over one newborn by pretending to cut the baby in half, revealing the true mother by her love.

answerHeadline: Elijah vs. Prophets of Baal — Fire From Heaven Soaks Water-Drenched Altar
modernSummary: Elijah challenges 450 prophets of Baal atop Mount Carmel: Baal stays silent all day, while fire from heaven licks up Elijah’s water-soaked wood, stones, and trench—followed later by God’s gentle whisper.

answerHeadline: Elijah Taken Up in a Chariot of Fire & Whirlwind
modernSummary: As Elijah walks beside Elisha across the parted Jordan River, blazing horses and a chariot of fire separate them and sweep Elijah into heaven without dying.

answerHeadline: Naaman Healed of Leprosy — Washing Seven Times in the Jordan River
modernSummary: A captive Israelite servant girl points Syrian army commander Naaman to Elisha; reluctant at first to bathe in the muddy Jordan River, Naaman dips seven times and his skin becomes clean like a child’s.

answerHeadline: Queen Esther — Brave Fasting “For Such a Time as This”
modernSummary: Orphan Jewish queen Esther risks death by approaching King Xerxes uninvited (“If I perish, I perish”) to expose wicked Haman’s plot and rescue her people.

answerHeadline: Job — Suffering Everything Lost, Patient Endurance & God in the Whirlwind
modernSummary: Wealthy righteous Job loses his children, wealth, and health in rapid tragedies yet refuses to curse God, debates miserable friends, and hears Yahweh answer out of a storm whirlwind before double restoration.

answerHeadline: Psalm 23 — “The Lord Is My Shepherd” & Valley of Shadow of Death
modernSummary: King David’s comforting song picturing God as a caring shepherd leading sheep beside green pastures, still waters, and safely through the dark valley of death.

answerHeadline: Ecclesiastes 3 — “A Time for Everything Under Heaven”
modernSummary: Solomon’s reflection that every season has its appointed time—a time to be born and die, weep and laugh, plant and uproot, silence and speak.

answerHeadline: Isaiah 53 & 6 — “Here Am I, Send Me” & Wounded Suffering Servant
modernSummary: Prophet Isaiah sees God high on a throne with six-winged seraphim (“Here am I! Send me”) and later foretells a gentle Servant pierced for our sins whose wounds heal us.

answerHeadline: Shadrach, Meshach & Abednego — Surviving the Blazing Fiery Furnace
modernSummary: Refusing to bow to King Nebuchadnezzar’s giant gold statue, three young Hebrews are tied up and thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter—yet a fourth figure walks with them and they emerge unburned without even smelling like smoke.

answerHeadline: King Nebuchadnezzar — Humbled Proud King Eating Grass Like a Cow
modernSummary: Boasting over Babylon’s skyline, proud King Nebuchadnezzar loses his mind for seven years—growing long hair like eagle feathers and eating grass like an ox in the fields until he honors heaven.

answerHeadline: Daniel in the Lions’ Den — Praying Three Times Daily & Shutting Lions’ Mouths
modernSummary: Arrested for praying openly by his open window despite a royal ban, faithful Daniel spends the night locked in a pit of hungry lions while an angel shuts their mouths without a scratch.

answerHeadline: Jonah — The Guy Swallowed / Eaten by a Whale (Great Fish)
modernSummary: Running away by ship from God’s call to preach in Nineveh, Jonah gets thrown overboard during a violent storm, gets swallowed alive by a giant whale / great fish for three days and nights, prays inside its belly, and gets spit onto dry land.

answerHeadline: Birth of Jesus — Bethlehem Manger, Shepherds, Angels & Three Wise Men
modernSummary: Mary and Joseph travel to Bethlehem where no room is left at the inn; baby Jesus is laid in a manger while angels sing to hillside shepherds and Eastern wise men follow a bright star bearing gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

answerHeadline: John the Baptist — Desert Preacher in Camel’s Hair Eating Locusts & Wild Honey
modernSummary: Living ruggedly in the Judean wilderness wearing itchy camel-hair clothes and a leather belt while eating locusts (bugs) and wild honey, John baptizes Jesus in the Jordan River as the Spirit descends like a dove.

answerHeadline: Jesus Tempted in the Wilderness 40 Days — Stones to Bread
modernSummary: After fasting forty days in the desert, Jesus rejects Satan’s three temptations—refusing to turn stones into bread, jump from the temple roof, or worship for earthly kingdoms.

answerHeadline: Wedding at Cana — First Miracle Turning Water Into Wine
modernSummary: When wine runs out at a village wedding in Cana, Mary tells servants to obey Jesus, who turns six giant stone jars of plain water into rich fine wine.

answerHeadline: Nicodemus & John 3:16 — “Born Again” Night Conversation
modernSummary: Pharisee leader Nicodemus sneaks over at night to question Jesus and hears “You must be born again” and “God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son.”

answerHeadline: Woman at the Well — “Living Water” in Samaria
modernSummary: At noon beside Jacob’s well, Jesus breaks cultural barriers by speaking with a Samaritan woman married five times, offering eternal living water and revealing Himself as Messiah.

answerHeadline: Sermon on the Mount — Beatitudes, Love Enemies & Lord’s Prayer
modernSummary: On a Galilean hillside Jesus teaches the Beatitudes (“Blessed are the meek / peacemakers”), turn the other cheek, “You are the salt and light,” the Lord’s Prayer, do not worry about tomorrow, and building on the rock.

answerHeadline: Walking on Water & Calming the Storm — Peter Steps Out of the Boat
modernSummary: Jesus quiets a raging sea storm (“Peace, be still!”) and later walks across storm waves at night—inviting Peter to walk on water until doubt makes Peter begin sinking and Jesus catches him.

answerHeadline: Feeding the 5,000 — Five Barley Loaves & Two Fish Multiplied
modernSummary: A little boy shares his lunch of five loaves of bread and two small fish; Jesus gives thanks and multiplies them to feed over five thousand hungry people with twelve baskets of leftovers.

answerHeadline: Woman Who Touched Jesus’ Robe — Healed After 12 Years of Bleeding
modernSummary: Suffering from twelve years of bleeding and rejected by crowds, a woman quietly reaches through the mob to touch the hem of Jesus’ cloak and is healed instantly.

answerHeadline: The Good Samaritan — Helping an Injured Stranger Left on the Road
modernSummary: When robbers beat a traveler half-dead along the Jericho road and religious leaders walk past, an outsider Samaritan bandages his wounds, puts him on his donkey, and pays the innkeeper.

answerHeadline: The Prodigal Son — Runaway Son Welcomed Home With Hug & Party
modernSummary: A rebellious younger son demands his inheritance early, wastes it all, ends up feeding pigs and starving—yet when he walks home ashamed, his father sprints to hug him, puts a robe and ring on him, and throws a feast.

answerHeadline: Raising of Lazarus — Dead Four Days & “Jesus Wept”
modernSummary: Dead and buried in a cave tomb for four days, Jesus’ friend Lazarus—brother of Mary and Martha—is called out alive wrapped in grave clothes after Jesus weeps with them.

answerHeadline: Zacchaeus — Short Tax Collector Who Climbed a Sycamore Tree
modernSummary: Too short to see over the crowd in Jericho, rich crooked tax collector Zacchaeus climbs up a sycamore tree—and Jesus looks up, invites Himself to dinner, and transforms his heart.

answerHeadline: Widow’s Two Small Copper Coins — Giving Everything She Had
modernSummary: Watching rich donors drop loud bags of gold into the temple treasury, Jesus honors a poor widow who quietly gives two tiny copper coins—all she had to live on.

answerHeadline: Peter — The Disciple Who Lied / Denied Knowing Jesus Three Times
modernSummary: Warmed by a courtyard charcoal fire after Jesus is arrested, apostle Simon Peter panics when recognized by a servant girl and repeatedly lies and swears three times, “I don’t know the man!” before the rooster crows twice and Jesus later forgives him by breakfast on the beach.

answerHeadline: Judas Iscariot — Betrayed Jesus With a Kiss for 30 Silver Coins
modernSummary: Disciple Judas Iscariot agrees to hand Jesus over for thirty pieces of silver, guiding armed guards into Gethsemane at night and identifying Jesus with a kiss.

answerHeadline: Crucifixion & Thief on the Cross — “Father, Forgive Them”
modernSummary: Condemned by Pilate, mocked with a crown of thorns, and nailed between two criminals on Calvary, Jesus prays “Father, forgive them,” tells a repentant thief “Today you will be with me in Paradise,” and finishes at noon darkness.

answerHeadline: Resurrection & Doubting Thomas — Empty Tomb & Touching Nail Scars
modernSummary: Three days after His burial, women find the stone rolled away and the empty tomb on Sunday dawn; later Jesus appears behind locked doors so doubting Thomas can see His nail-scarred hands and side.

answerHeadline: Pentecost — Wind, Tongues of Fire & Speaking Every Language
modernSummary: Fifty days after Passover, a rushing wind fills the upper room, tongues like fire rest on Jesus’ followers, and they boldly proclaim God’s wonders in every visitor’s native language.

answerHeadline: Stephen — First Christian Martyr Seeing Heaven Open While Stoned
modernSummary: Radiant with heaven’s glory as an angry crowd stones him outside Jerusalem while young Saul holds their coats, deacon Stephen prays “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them.”

answerHeadline: Saul / Paul on the Damascus Road — Blinding Light & Scales Falling From Eyes
modernSummary: Hunting Christians toward Damascus, furious Saul is knocked down by blinding noon light as Jesus asks “Why are you persecuting me?”—blinded three days until Ananias prays and scales fall from his eyes.

answerHeadline: Paul & Silas Singing in Midnight Prison Earthquake
modernSummary: Locked in inner prison stocks at midnight in Philippi, Paul and Silas pray and sing hymns out loud until a sudden earthquake shakes all doors open and the terrified jailer believes with his whole family.

answerHeadline: Eutychus — Boy Who Fell Asleep & Dropped Out a Third-Story Window
modernSummary: While Paul preaches late past midnight in an upstairs lamp-lit room in Troas, young Eutychus dozes off on a third-floor windowsill, plunges three stories down, and is raised alive by Paul.

answerHeadline: 1 Corinthians 13 — “Love Is Patient, Love Is Kind”
modernSummary: Paul’s famous wedding and life hymn describing agape love: patient, kind, never envious or boastful, keeping no record of wrongs—faith, hope, and love remain, and the greatest is love.

answerHeadline: Armor of God — Belt of Truth, Shield of Faith & Sword of the Spirit
modernSummary: To stand firm against spiritual darkness, Paul pictures putting on God’s full armor: belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shoes of peace, shield of faith, helmet of salvation, and Scripture as sword.

answerHeadline: Fruit of the Spirit — Love, Joy, Peace, Patience, Kindness…
modernSummary: Growing out of life with the Holy Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.

answerHeadline: Hebrews 11 — “Hall of Faith” & Cloud of Witnesses
modernSummary: Defines faith as certainty of things hoped for, then celebrates Abel, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Moses, Rahab, Gideon, and David before cheering believers on to run the race looking to Jesus.

answerHeadline: Revelation 21–22 — New Heaven, New Earth & “No More Tears”
modernSummary: On the final pages of the Bible, God creates a new heaven and new earth, wipes every tear from human eyes, banishes death and pain forever, and flows the crystal River of Life beside the Tree of Life.
